description: Come join us at Carolingian Dance Practice! The winter/spring 2026 practices will be on fourth Tuesdays: Feb 24, Mar 24, Apr 28, and May 26. This is a fun social occasion for all: an evening where we all get together to learn Renaissance Dances and socialize with the members of the Barony. It is specifically newcomer-friendly: all dances are taught, you don’t need to come with a partner (we encourage folks to switch partners from dance to dance), and folks generally come in street clothes. Just wear something comfortable that you can move in (especially comfortable shoes). We meet from 7:30 – 9:30pm at the Holy Trinity Armenian Church, at 145 Brattle Street in Cambridge. There’s a parking lot for those who need to drive, bus routes nearby, and it’s less than a 20 minute walk from the Harvard Square MBTA station. The parking lot is off of Sparks Street, on the far side of the Church away from Brattle Street. (If using a GPS, 62 Sparks Street is roughly across the street from the parking lot.) The hall where we will be dancing is next to the parking lot, so if you are walking up Brattle Street, turn onto Sparks Street to get to the hall. If the front door on Sparks Street is locked, come around to the parking lot side and use the door there. Dances are taught and called using the gender-free “Larks and Robins” style, popular with many of the local dance communities. We have a lot of space (easily twice what we need for dancing), so folks are welcome to come bring other SCA activities for the sidelines, or even to just come hang out! The site costs $100 per session; donations are optional, but welcome to help defray the cost of renting the hall. So come join us! description: Kingdom of Atenveldt Fall 2026 Crown Tournament Greetings and salutations to the populace of the Solar Kingdom of Atenveldt. On September 18 th through the 20 th , the Barony March of Mons Tonitrus shall host our Kingdom’s Fall Crown Tournament at the Holy Trinity Monastery Center in Saint David, AZ. All Attendees are encouraged to bring banners, displays, and any items to enhance the pageantry of the event. Pre-registration is open until 11:59 on September 14 th , 2026. Pre-registration link: Pre-reg Weekend: $25 for members and $35 for non-members ($30 / $40 at Gate) Pre-reg Day: $20 for members and $30 for non-members ($25 / $35 at Gate) Friday, Sep 18: Gate open from 2pm – 8pm Game Night Saturday, Sep 19: Gate open from 8am – 6pm Fall Crown Tournament, Youth Activities and a Drum Cricle Sunday, Sep 20: Gate open from 8am – 10am Warlord Tournament, Queen’s Rapier Champion, Kingdom Archery Champion and Kingdom Thrown Weapons Champion Site Information: The Holy Trinity Monastery Center is located at 1605 S St Marys Way, Saint David, AZ 85630. The property was founded in 1974 as a Benedictine Monastery in the Olivetan tradition. The 132-acre monastery was dissolved in 2017, and now hosts group and private retreats, and offers facilities for classes, workshops, conferences, and weddings. Also on the property are an auditorium, an adobe chapel, a library, and several artesian-fed ponds. Site has shade trees, stone privies, porta-potties, on-site water spigots, and roll-off trash service. Camping is discreetly wet, staking is allowed, and above ground fire pits in designated areas are permitted (with extinguisher). There is an on-site Gift Shop and Coffee Shop (limited hours). ADA Stone privies and porta johns with hand washing. A limited number of on-site accommodations are available for rent, including lodging, and full and partial RV hook-ups for a fee. Limited Dry RV sites are available for no charge. Please contact the site to reserve on-site accommodations, including full and partial hookup RV spaces ( ). Benson and Tombstone are the closest towns with hotels/motels. The Benson Hospital is 11 miles away. There is a Dollar General 2 miles away in Saint David, and a Walmart and Safeway in Benson, within 15 minutes. Closest gas is in Benson. Site Website: Merchant Information: Merchants are required to preregister and pay appropriate member or nonmember fees for themselves and support staff. Merchant fees are asked to provide a donation of an item or items for the Volunteer Raffle. Prospective Merchants please contact Lord Kerwyn at for coordination. Directions: From Tucson – East on Interstate 10, off at either Exits 303 or 304 in Benson, South on Highway 80 (Tombstone & Douglas) to St. David (approximately 8 miles) – Holy Trinity Monastery Center is located south of St. David between Mile Post 302 and 303. From the East – Get off I-10 at Exit 306 – travel west in Benson to pick up Highway 80, follow above directions. Your Event Stewards are Lord Kerwyn Cnoic an Mhadhaidh () and Lady Ysolde Eileen de Lorraine ()

description: Event Steward SCA Name: Ceara of Morven Event Steward contacts: Event Name: West Kingdom Equestrian Championship Event Site Open: Sep 20, 9am Event Site Close: Sep 20, 5pm Further Event Information: Come one, come all to learn about Equestrian activities, witness impressive feats of horsemanship, and participate in the selection of our next Kingdom Champion. Our Current Equestrian Champion, Christopher O Mulryan, challenges all riders within or without the Kingdom, unless they be enemies of Their Majesties, to attend and display their Prowess and Franchise upon the field. Specific challenges will be announced in the West Kingdom Equestrian Facebook page but traditionally encompass games of martial skill (challenge course, head, reeds, rings, etc.) and opportunities to demonstrate formal horsemanship (patterns of some type). Onsite camping is not available, but several locations nearby provide accommodations for horses and their owners. title: Gyldenholt Anniversary
location: Cedar Grove Park, 11385 Pioneer Rd, Tustin, CA 92782, USA
description: By invitation of their Excellencies Baron Brynjólfr Brandsson and Baroness Dyrfinna Drengsdottir of Gyldenholt, we bid ye gather with us when the sun reaches its zenith and the days stretch long over our golden groves for this grand day where the flames of the forge meet the fire of the soul at the Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . Gather round, ye fighters of flame and artisans of pungent root. A call to glory rings out, bidding the bold to bring forth their finest, for the fervor of competition beckons. Their Excellencies will seek Champions in the following categories: Combat: Armored, Rapier, Cut & Thrust, and Youth Champions Arts & Sciences: The Barony of Gyldenholt Annual Arts & Sciences Champion Bardic: The Barony of Gyldenholt Annual Bardic Champion Awards: The Motley Mêlée Theatre: Best Fiery Performance The Paramour of Picante: Spiciest Complement on the Tourney Field Best Use of Spices & Herbs in an Arts & Sciences Entry: All Categories Welcome As we are blithe on this day to celebrate all periods from Greek to Norse to Ottoman to Tudor, we bid you dress in your finest fiery attire of sun gold, bold crimson, and delicious saffron. “I hope for dear summertime; wait - be willing in favour of me; smile, love, smile.” ~ Inscription on a 15th Century Saddle SCHEDULE: 8am: Site Open 10:00am: Opening Court - at Their Majesty’s pleasure Lists close 15 minutes after the end of Opening Court - fighting will start shortly thereafter 11:30am: Arts & Sciences competition drop-off period ends & populace voting begins Children’s Activities Will Be Between Rounds 12pm – 1pm: Bardic Competition under the Baronial Pavilion- fighters can arrange time with Their Excellencies, as needed 1pm – 2pm: Artisan Showcase under the Arts Ramada 2pm - 3pm: Theatrical Scene Performances under the Baronial Pavilion 4pm: Closing Court - approximate time depending on combat finals 6pm: Site closes ARTS & SCIENCES COMPETITION for the Baronial Arts & Sciences Champion . The entries do not need to adhere to the theme of the day but it is appreciated if they do. Entries should be displayed under the Arts Ramada by 11:30am. BARDIC COMPETITION for the Baronial Bardic Champion . The bardic pieces do not need to adhere to the theme of the day, but it is appreciated if they do. Due to allotted time, we ask that the bardic pieces be no more than 3 minutes in length. COMBAT SCENARIOS: For Rapier and Armored Combatants: This year, your challenge shall be… spiciest compliment on the tourney field to win the Paramour of Picante Award ! In honor of the theme of the day, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice , a special benefit will be given to those on the tourney field when offering a compliment to an esteemed opponent. Have your flattery and wit at the ready! - Scenario: Single Elimination, 1 Spicy Complement = 1 Extra Life Bonus - Spicy Compliment Bonus: 1 Per Tournament IMPORTANT: In order to earn the Extra Life Bonus, you must issue your compliment *prior* to exiting the field following a loss. After the bonus is received, compliments may be administered liberally at thine discretion for the remainder of the tournament. Youth Combat is scheduled to begin after the 4th round of Armored Fighting. A Youth Champion will be chosen based on the most honorable and chivalrous combatant. ACTIVITIES: The Motley Mêlée Theater Award: Time limit: 2 minutes for 1 performer, 3 minutes for 2 performers, and a max of 5 minutes for 3 or more performers. Performances must be PG rated and suitable to a family audience. To be performed in the Baronial Pavillion. It is not a requirement that these scenes be drawn from period pieces but more inspired by medieval life. Shakespeare is always welcome but you may draw from modern pieces, dramatic and humorous, such as Elizabeth, The Merchant of Venice, Men In Tights, The Court Jester, Monty Python, The Princess Bride, etc. We only ask you to stick to the theme of the day, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . The award will be for Best Fiery Performance . Best Use of an Herb or Spice Award: All categories are welcome! Baroness Dyrfinna challenges the populace to have fun and play with our theme of the day by incorporating the spirit of herbs and spices into your dress, decor, or feast table for the day. If you’ve “cooked” up something special, please bring it to Her Excellency’s attention as she makes her progress. As Her Excellency will be selecting the winner, please refrain from using ginger or jasmine in any submission due to allergy . Herbal Craft Activity: Our Baroness Dyrfinna graciously invites the populace to join her for a craft activity of card making with elements of period spices, plants, and flowers. Please join us under the Arts Ramada for this lovely activity, children are most welcome! Arts & Sciences Competition and Display: Please set up your item(s) for display at one of the tables under the Arts Ramada by 11:30am. We will have a 1 hour artisan showcase from 1pm to 2pm. All artisans are asked to participate by coming to the Arts Pavilion and stand with their art and discuss. Arts entries can also include what you are wearing for the day or heraldic/decorative display at your pavilion, if it fits the theme, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . If this is the case for your entry, please provide a paper with at least your name, a description of your entry (and ideally a photo of said entry) at the display table during the competition and, if possible, be present for the artisan showcase. Please note, Arts & Sciences entries do not need to follow the theme of the day. The entries do not require documentation, but it is encouraged. MERCHANTS: Merchants are welcome however, you must provide for your own city license and insurance. Please contact the Stewards in advance to let us know you are coming. EVENT REGISTRATION: Adult Event Registration: $25. Adult Member Discount Event Registration: $15. Children 17 and under are guests of the Barony. Cash and checks accepted at the gate. Please make checks payable to “SCA Inc./Barony of Gyldenholt”. Please Note: This is a dry site. PARKING: Parking at the park is limited, please unload and then park at Pioneer Middle School. EVENT STEWARDS: Madame Cyrana Chardon d’Argent & Baroness Ceridwen Killian EVENT EMAIL: -caid.org DIRECTIONS: From the North – Take your best route to I-5 South. Exit 101A Tustin Ranch Rd. and turn left. Go approximately 2.5 miles and turn left onto Pioneer Way. Turn right onto Pioneer Rd. The park entrance will be on the left. From the South – Take your best route to I-5 North. Exit 101A Tustin Ranch Rd. and turn left. Go approximately 2.5 miles and turn left onto Pioneer Way. Turn right onto Pioneer Rd. The park entrance will be on the left

description: The beach cities of the Barony of Lyondemere invite you to escape the summer heat and join Gareth and Alatiel, Baron and Baroness, at the beach to celebrate our 48th Anniversary! While our current understanding of a “beach day” is based in 19th century leisure activities, many of our global ancestors found time to relax and play along the many bodies of water found around the world, from the lakes and rivers of medieval Europe to the seasides of ancient Rome to the oceans of the seafaring cultures of the Pasifika. Celebrate with us in the cooler beach weather of Lyondemere as we choose our champions in Arts and Sciences, Heavy Armored Combat, Rapier, and Cut and Thrust combat. SCHEDULE 8 AM - Site Open 10 AM - Opening Court, or at their Excellencies’ pleasure 4 PM - Closing Court, or at their Excellencies’ pleasure 5 PM - Site Closes REGISTRATION INFORMATION: $25 Adult Event Registration, $15 Adult Member Discount Event Registration (with proof of membership). For our Rapier and Cut and Thrust tournaments - in most popular depictions, seafaring swordfighters (more commonly known as pirates) are depicted with missing body parts, so this will be a “wounds retained” tournament where “injuries” from previous rounds are carried over to the next bouts. On Saturday, July 18, 2026, our Kingdom shall meet at the crossroads of great trade routes, kick the sand from our boots at Mid East Feast, let our silk banners fly, and spend a day wrapped in the luxury of Al-Andalusian frivolity. All are cordially invited to don their finest caftans and veils to celebrate the food inspired by the union of Spain and Arabia. Expect a comfortable experience filled with the sensations of drumbeats and coinbelts clinking as Middle Eastern musicians and dancers provide spectacle between the courses of a great meal provided by our dedicated cooks, led by the extraordinary Lord Percival of the Tea House. The menu features a starter course of fresh fruits, breads, and cheeses to be followed by Ahsa (soup), Qar (Zucchini topped with almonds), Badhinjan Mutajjan (oven-roasted eggplant), Djajat Uumrus (chicken), Mirkas (sausages of Lamb and Eggplant, Chicken with couscous) to end with a desert of Mu’assal (honey pudding) and an assortment of cookies and pastries. Guests are invited to bring their finest period board games to play and share amongst their tables. Chess may have originated in India but it had to pass through the Middle East to reach Europe. Site is dry, no smoking, ADA accessible, only registered service animals allowed, no weapons. Directions are: make your best way to the intersection of Shea Blvd. and State Rt. 87. description: Steward:Lady Sorcha ingen ui Chainnigh Email: As the days grow colder and winter prepares to encompass the land, let us celebrate Midwinter - with a Hunt. A final chance to collect the bounty of the wilderness to see us through until spring. Bring your bows and join our roving round where we will shoot at various animal targets including rabbits, foxes, birds, boar and (pending Crown permission) deer. Combat arrows only as some targets are moving. There with also be a forging challenge where we will collect the wild harvest, with participants rewarded depending on how much they gather and a prize for the highest bounty. As the sun sets we shall then retire to Dolphin's Keep for feasting, dancing and to admire the entries into our Arts and Sciences competitions. Our two categories are as follows: 1. Creatures of the Wild - in tribute to our quarry present an item themed around an animal or animals of the wilderness. 2. Hunting/Traveling supplies - one should never go into the wild unprepared. Present an item that would be taken and used when hunting or traveling. We hope you will join us for our foray into the wild before the bitter chill of winter forces us all back inside. As we enjoy the comfort of our Keep we must not forget the earth and her bounty that nurtures us, so we may bid her good rest until spring. As this event is hosted by a group based in the state of Victoria, please remember that anyone carrying or using any kind of sword in the state - including visitors and those passing through - must carry proof that they have completed the Victorian weapons exemption application process with the SCA Ltd Registrar - see for detailed information

description: Perfectly Period Feast (or Plausibly Period Feast), known as PPF, is a feasting event that creates as period as possible immersion in a particular time and place. Our first ever PPF in Caid is recreating the Ottoman Empire at the height of Suleiman the Magnificent’s reign in the 1550s. WHEN: Saturday, August 22, 2026 from 2-9 PM WHERE: St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, 122 California Ave, Monrovia CA 91016 The food and style of service will be Ottoman, the garb will be Ottoman, the music will be Ottoman, everything will all blend together to create historical immersion to the best of our ability. To that end, we ask that attendees also come prepared to contribute to this wonderful experience. Please come attired appropriately, prepared for handwashing ceremonies, sitting down on sumptuous rugs and pillows, eating 20 dishes of 16th century Ottoman food with one’s fingers, and enjoying the ambience and company. description: Additional Notes on Pet Policy: Pets must be on a leash and you must clean up after them. Royal Progress: Scarlet Guard Inn XI Shire of Hunters Home June 5, 2026, 3pm June 7, 2026, 1pm Fraternal Order of Eagles #965 1050 Eagle’s Nest Road Brockway PA 15824 Greetings archers and throwers! The Order of the Scarlet Guard and the Shire of Hunters Home invite you to attend the eleventh Scarlet Guard Inn Archery Festival. As with years past, there is a lot going on over this weekend, so here are the highlights! Archery! The main attraction is, of course, the archery. We can’t wait until Saturday to begin, so the annual Flight Shoot will be Friday evening. Saturday will see a smorgasbord of options, as we already have slated a bunch of novelty ranges, a couple woods walks, a clout range, and of course the Scarlet Guard Challenge. Speaking of which… The Scarlet Guard Challenge! Any group with a seneschal can send one archer as a representative, as long as the archer is not a member of the Scarlet Guard, equivalent, or higher Order. Anyone who has previously won the Scarlet Guard Challenge is likewise ineligible to compete again. Once a group has chosen their archer, please contact Master Juan Miguel Cezar () with the name of the group being represented, the name of the seneschal, and the name of the archer no later than June 3, 2026. For the tournament itself, archers MUST bring a letter signed by the seneschal declaring them as the chosen representative of that group, as well as a small prize to be added to a gift basket which will be presented to the winner along with the ancestral banner which bears the name of all past winners and the groups they have represented. Thrown Weapons! We already support the flinging of wood and metal through the air, regardless of its shape, but this year brings something special. It has been declared that the Aethelmearc Thrown Weapons Champion will be determined at the Scarlet Guard Inn! Throw for fun! Throw for glory! (Or both, both is good) Bardic! Come enjoy the camaraderie and entertainment of our bardic circle tradition. Whether it is under the roof of the big pavilion or gathering around our large fire ring, each night everyone is encouraged to help fill the air with songs and stories. Merchants! Hunters Home invites merchants to set up their wares at no additional charge. We had many great items for sale at our last event. Please inform the autocrat so that we can reserve space for you. Camping! Camping is free! Please feel free to stay Friday and Saturday night. There is plenty of camping space. Some already have regular spots, but it IS first come first serve. There is space for RVs but it is limited and there are no hookups and no dumping allowed, please contact the autocrat ahead of time. We have a community campfire that everyone is welcome to join, but if you choose to have your own campfire that is fine as long as you leave the site as you found it. The Tavern! The Food: There will be no feast at this event, however there will be a modest sideboard open Friday evening and throughout the day on Saturday in the tavern. The Games: Want to compete off the range as well? Two gaming tables will be set aside in the tavern with an assortment of games to choose from. We welcome any additions. In addition to the bardic offerings, period games have proven to be a popular way to spend the evenings. Some general notes: -Your equipment will need to be inspected before engaging in martial activities, so please give yourself time to get inspected. -The site is discreetly wet. Just make sure you clean up any messes and leave the site as you found it. -Being June in Pennsylvania, and since this site isn’t conveniently close to any major shopping areas, be prepared for any weather. This means both sunscreen and some way to stay warm through the night. -Bug and tick spray! We had a good long freeze this winter, so maybe they won’t be as bad this year, but it’s better safe than sorry. The schedule as it currently stands: Friday 3pm Site Opens 7pm Flight Shoot Saturday 9am Troll Opens 10am Morning Court 10am – after court – All ranges open. 11am Qualifier for Thrown Weapons Championships begins 3pm Thrown Weapons Championships finals 345pm Ranges close 4pm Scarlet Guard Challenge 5pm Awards Ceremony and Royal Court Sunday 12pm Site Closes This schedule is subject to change Adult Event Registration is $30, Adult Member Discount Event Registration is $20, Children 6-17: $5, Children 5 and under: Free. Make checks payable to SCA-PA, Inc. – Shire of Hunters Home. Reservations may be sent to the Autocrat. AUTOCRAT for this event will be Thorfinnr y Elsfiord (Tod Elford) -AUTOCRAT is Alrekr Bergsson (David Bessler)

description: FACEBOOK EVENT PAGE Event Steward SCA Name: Deirdre the Difficult Event Steward contacts: Event Name: Spring Offensive Event Site Open: May 22, 10am Event Site Close: May 25, 12pm Further Event Information: The Barony of Selviergard will be hosting their Spring Offensive and Baronial Investiture. Planned activities include: Baron Colum’s Court Friday evening, The Baron Erik’s Bardic Fyre Friday night. Saturday will have Baronial Investiture Court,Bardic Horn Competition and Investiture Feast (Don’t forget your ingredients list). Fighting Scenarios for Saturday, Pas De Arms for both Rapier and Hard Suit and several scenarios for both Hard Suit and Rapier involving the Raiding and Pillaging of villages will be held on Sunday. IKAC archery shoot. A White Stage Hunt is also planned. THE CALL OF THE NORTH: THE SELVIERGARD ARTISAN CHALLENGE ⚔️ Hale and hearty greetings, Selviergard! The winds of the North are rising, and the scent of the forge and the loom is in the air. As your MoAS, I am calling a Hird of Artisans to gather for a Viking A&S Challenge! This is no mere gathering for finished treasures; I want to see your Works in Progress (WIPs), your half-carved dreams, and the ink-stained scrolls of your research. Whether your craft is born of the forge, leather, bone, or loom; whether you work in fiber, story, or song—if your heart beats for the age of the Northmen (8th–11th Century), your work has a place at our hearth! 🎨 The Challenge of the Three Hues To prove your fealty to Selviergard, your work must bear the mark of our home. We challenge every maker to find a way to include our three colors directly into the project itself: • 🟡 Or (Gold): For the sun that guides our longships. • 🔴 Gules (Red): For the fire of the hearth and the blood of the brave. • ⚫ Sable (Black): For the iron of our blades and the deep winter night. I, too, shall be working at the bench! I will have my own project on display to serve as inspiration and to spark the fires of craft, though I shall not be competing for the prize. My work stands only to honor the hall and encourage your hands! The People’s Choice: Word-Glory! The All-Father watches, but so does the populace! We shall hold a People’s Choice Award where every soul in the Barony may cast their vote for the work that stirs their spirit. The victor shall take home the glory of the folk and a name that shall ring through the mead hall! Please direct any question to Niall De Exeter (Nathan Meadows) Viking Games Saturday and Sunday. description: Steward:Baroness Kathelyne Berghart Email: TL: DR – An evening of trivia and entertainment as we celebrate 25 years of St Florian de la Riviere. Please join us in celebrating St Florian de la Riviere’s silver anniversary in style. We invite the populace to dress in their best purple and white or add a splash of purple to your favourite outfit in the form of a ribbon, sash or accessory. We would love for anyone with personal banners to lend them to the event – a collection will be organised prior so that the event team can dress the hall. Objects will be photographed and will be able to be collected at the end of the event. A delightful arrangement of finger food will be provided, with memorable tastes from the annals of St Florian’s cooking history

description: Steward:Nathan Blacktower Email: Website: Greetings, noble travellers, Embark on a journey to the far western reaches of Lochac for an unforgettable weekend of medieval immersion at Western Raids! Join like-minded friends in a realm of adventure where the echoes of the past come alive. Discover the Silk Road Markets: Step into a vibrant marketplace filled with treasures and delights inspired by the Silk Road. Browse through a myriad of wares, savour exotic treats, and immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of medieval craftsmanship. Feats of Prowess and Competitions: Witness and partake in epic tournaments and displays of skill that will transport you back to an age of chivalry and honour. Engage in friendly competition, showcase your prowess, and claim glory on the battlefield. Entertainment Beyond Imagining: Delight in the merriment of singing, dancing, and a myriad of medieval activities that will captivate your senses. Attend classes to hone your skills or learn ancient arts, ensuring that every moment is filled with enchantment. Bardic Tales by the Fire: As the sun sets, gather around the flickering flames to share your best Bardic tales, songs, or performances. Warm your spirit with the camaraderie of fellow travellers and let the tales of old weave a spellbinding atmosphere. Bookings Officer Assistance: For our esteemed travellers, our diligent bookings officer awaits your arrival to assist with any arrangements. Ensure a seamless experience by checking in and letting us cater to your needs with the utmost care and hospitality. Join us for a weekend where medieval history takes over, forge memories that will last a lifetime. Western Raids beckon, and the adventure awaits! May your journey be swift and your heart filled with the spirit of medieval revelry! More details will be available on the Western Raids website
